correctness.rationale: In the stated normalization the central H commutes with every noise conjugation, the dissipative law stays diagonal, and measurement after coherent evolution convolves that law with the central probability Q_s. Central Fourier transforms are scalar with factors exp(-gamma*t*(1-r_lambda)) and kappa_lambda respectively. Counting-measure Plancherel gives the claimed 1/n! prefactor and nonnegative deficit. At finite t the classical factors are positive in every mode. Equality forces unit absolute value of every scalar transform of Q_s, including the trivial one, so Plancherel gives squared mass one. The resulting single atom is central and hence the identity for n>=3. Since the coherent operator is a convolution, its identity column being a phase times the identity basis vector forces scalarity. For the period the content gaps for n=3,4 have gcd 3,2; for n>=5 the three displayed partitions exist and have gaps n, 2(n-1), 3(n-1), of gcd one. Dividing the normalized denominator C by that gcd gives the least period in units of 2*pi. For the curvature, the transposition amplitudes at leading order are -i*delta/C and H^2(e,e)=1/C; real H makes each Q_delta(g) even. Thus Q_delta=delta_e+(delta^2/C)(mu_2-delta_e)+O(delta^4), giving exactly the stated K_n, positive because the standard mode has positive spectral gap. At t=0 the physical phase is zero; the fixed-t deficit function has the stated expansion in its formal phase variable. For bounded corroboration, independently assembled 6- and 24-dimensional matrices at gamma=0.7, t=0.8 (index (g,h) receives 1/C for each tau with g=tau*h) gave revival Frobenius errors below 1e-14 and positive deficits 0.193350989 and 0.263066558 at half the respective periods. At delta=0.004 the divided deficits were 0.168669855 and 0.098016012 versus analytic coefficients 0.168670687 and 0.098016258. Uploaded verify.py and its recorded PASS were inspected, not rerun; proof, not this bounded test, gives the all-n result.
